title: Rondonia: forest clearing seen as a drop in HV
finding: Negative result: OPERA DIST-ALERT shows new disturbance on 5.75 % of the box, but the 4x-wobble HV test on display-scaled GIBS tiles flags none of it. Calibrated GCOV HV is needed here.

sections.what: Forest in Rondonia is cleared and burned in the dry season. The box is where OPERA DIST-ALERT showed the most vegetation disturbance in late Oct 2026.
sections.why: L-band HV is volume scattering from branches and trunks; when the canopy is cut, HV drops by several dB, through smoke and cloud.
sections.radar: Same track 068 descending, 2026-08-29 vs 2026-10-28 (about 2 months). A pixel is flagged when its HV (green channel) falls more than 4x the 12-day wobble of 2026-08-17 to 2026-08-29.
sections.validation: The radar test flagged nothing: the quiet-pair HV wobble in GIBS display values is large (sigma 34.1), so a 4x threshold is 136.4 units. OPERA DIST-ALERT marks 5.75 % of the box as new disturbance in the same window, so agreement is 0 %: this method misses it.
sections.limits: Display-scaled GIBS radar, not calibrated dB; screening only. The quiet pair spans 12 days but the event pair 60 days, so seasonal drying also lowers HV. DIST is optical and misses cloudy days.
